capabilities.name: Independent OMS-vs-ledger reconciliation with typed blocking reports

Blocking anomalies consistently drive a Mismatch or Unavailable status; OMS raises FillContentConflict instead of silently dropping a reused execution id. Mismatch and Unavailable drive a sticky reconciliation_blocked inside the authority through RiskCheck::Reconciliation, cleared only by an authenticated operator resolution. capabilities.name: Deterministic permit-to-intent digest binding with durable single-use permits
capabilities.evidence_status: IMPLEMENTED, NOT VERIFIED; no commit SHA, CI run or independent verification is claimed here. trading-core carries `permit_digest`, a domain-separated SHA-256 over a canonical JSON preimage naming the reservation identity fields carried by PermitRef plus the complete OrderIntent. RiskAuthority::permit_digest exposes it for a committed Reservation; OmsStore::create recomputes it from its stored intent and rejects a mismatch with typed OmsError::PermitDigestMismatch. A journal-backed consumed-permit BTreeSet is replayed on recovery: identical replay with the same client order id is an idempotent no-op, a spent permit with a new client id is denied with OmsError::PermitAlreadyConsumed, and a tampered intent or rewritten permit identity is denied. Dedicated falsifier tests cover each case and restart replay. This is an unkeyed integrity binding only: real signed permits, KMS/IAM keys, production identity and a deployed independent risk service remain BLOCKED pending owner authorization; no authenticity, cryptographic signature or live-readiness claim is granted.

capabilities.name: Immutable bar-cadence and annualisation experiment contract
capabilities.evidence_status: Pre-registration now requires bar kind, fixed or explicitly not-applicable interval, timestamp semantics, versioned calendar and session definition, named annualisation basis with a consistent period count, and a point-in-time basis that bounds what the boolean certifies. A pure cadence validator fails closed on ordered timestamps that disagree with a daily or minute registration, on a synthetic dataset without a synthetic calendar and fixed interval, and on calendar metadata that is missing or inconsistent for a market dataset; it never invents bars for calendar gaps. Registered searches use only the declared periods_per_year, reject conflicting CLI values, require an explicit execution-latency model and use null/not_evaluated states for unexamined holdout fields. capabilities.name: Generalized calendar-based bar-cadence validation
capabilities.evidence_status: IMPLEMENTED, NOT REAL-MARKET VERIFIED; no commit SHA, CI run or independent verification is claimed here. All calendar artifacts are checked-in TEST_FIXTURE files; no real-market calendar validator is claimed, and a fixture cannot certify MARKET origin or exchange-calendar validity. Registrations now require explicit dataset_origin (SYNTHETIC or MARKET) bound to the dataset manifest, bar_timezone, bar_anchor aligned with timestamp_semantics, and a versioned calendar reference with a digest recomputed from a checked-in artifact. quantlab.experiments.calendar resolves caller-supplied calendar artifacts with no database, service or network; D11 retired the checked-in synthetic calendar fixtures; unknown identifiers, wrong digests and conflicting declarations fail closed. Session artifacts model regular sessions, auction exclusion, scheduled breaks, early closes, holidays and an overnight session; the validator compares observations with the expected scheduled UTC timestamps instead of one fixed elapsed interval, accepts fixture calendar gaps, rejects missing sessions or bars, and does not invent or forward-fill a bar inside a fixture-bounded check. Explicit coverage statuses (no_trade, not_listed, suspended, halted, market_closed, missing) keep an absent price as None; those statuses are not authority-checked and the search adapter does not pass them as an integrated workflow. Named annualisation bases fix bar family, bar_interval_ns and periods_per_year (daily 252, NSE cash one-minute 94500, five-minute 18900, fifteen-minute 6300); the CLI cannot override them. Nineteen new cadence tests plus the existing registry suite pass locally. No provider observation or licensed data was used; all rights remain UNKNOWN. Claim scope: evidence/M4-2-1-CLAIM-SCOPE-2026-11-22.md narrows M4.2.1 to implemented, not real-market verified. Falsifiers: a fixture calendar marked synthetic:false certifies MARKET origin; an expected schedule generated from observed first and last timestamps passes a missing first or last bar without independent manifest coverage bounds; a close-anchored inclusive 09:15-15:30 session yields 376 bars while the registered one-minute basis fixes 375 bars per session and 94500 periods per year, leaving bar-open/close schedule math undefined or the period count unbound. No real-market calendar validator, source completeness, alpha, profitability, venue-realism or live-readiness claim.
